children: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar amid mixed signals. Financial markets appear to have been caught in a "tug-of-war between risk-on momentum in U.S. technology shares and a cascade of geopolitical headwinds emanating from Europe and the Middle East," UOB's Global Economics & Markets Research team says in a research report. For today, Taiwan's September export orders will be closely watched as "markets assess the durability of the AI investment cycle, which has supported growth in economies such as South Korea, Singapore and Malaysia," the team adds. The U.S. dollar edges 0.1% higher to 158.58 yen, but is little changed at 1.2793 Singapore dollars while the Australian dollar is flat at US$0.6976, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
